svg.title: rocketmq-broker architecture
svg.desc: The broker binary resolves its command line and configuration file into a ValidatedBrokerConfig, hands it with a service context and telemetry to the Builder, and BrokerBootstrap moves through the Configured, Initialized and Running states before readiness is published. BrokerRuntime composes a request pipeline, a data plane, a control plane and metadata. The normal listener, the fast listener and the embedded ProxyBrokerFacade share one dispatcher, which applies admission, authentication and authorization, routes by request code and applies fast failure. Twenty processor types handle send, pull, POP and ACK, transaction, client and consumer, query, lite and admin requests. Processors reach the message store of rocketmq-store through the EscapeBridge; the store is a local file store by default, with optional RocksDB and tiered storage. Metadata managers hold topics, queue mappings, subscription groups, offsets, filters, order information and client sessions. Deferred requests park pull, POP, notification and POP lite long polling until a message arrives or the wait expires. Background services deliver scheduled and timer messages, check transactions, revive POP messages and run scheduled tasks. The control plane registers with the NameServer through BrokerOuterAPI, follows an optional Controller and synchronizes a replica from its master. The store replicates to the peer Broker of the same broker name. ServiceLifecycle provides probes and the shutdown deadline, and telemetry is exported when configured. The startup journal lists the components in the order start-up completes them, and the shutdown order lists the phases of a stop. Where motion is allowed, a looping tour plays eight steps: boot, register, send, consume, background, replicate, operate and shut down.
svg.text: Bootstrap, request dispatch and owned services of one Broker process.
